description: Send a notification to a topic. Reusing an id while the previous one is still open updates it instead of making a new one.

actions.description: Optional buttons, each with one of reply, url, http or broadcast. Answer buttons: [{"label":"Yes","reply":"yes"},{"label":"No","reply":"no"}]; wait_for_reply returns the tapped one as answer. Add "text":true to one reply button to let the human type an answer (at most 1000 characters), returned as text. http and broadcast need the topic's device_actions on (set_topic).

broadcast.description: Android broadcast: {intent (the app's default if empty), extras}

clear.description: Clear the notification after the button runs

http.description: Request the reader's device sends: {method (POST if empty), url, headers, body}

text.description: On one reply button: the human types an answer, returned by wait_for_reply as text

color.description: Optional card color as #RRGGBB, shown as a bar; the user's color_rules (settings) win over it

devices.description: Optional: only these devices alert (names or ids from devices, at most 20); every other reader lists it silently

format.description: markdown (default) or text, which is shown exactly as sent

icon.description: Optional http(s) image URL shown with the notification; the topic's icon when omitted

id.description: Optional stable key (external_id), e.g. disk-build. Use it later with resolve(topic, external_id).

live.description: Optional: send only to ntfy streams open now and keep nothing (no inbox, no replay, no buttons to answer)

repeat.description: Optional: alert again every this long (1m to 24h, e.g. 5m) until someone acknowledges, snoozes, dismisses or resolves it

repeat_times.description: How many times to repeat at most (default 10)

name: send

description: List notifications.

state.description: open (default), all, active, acknowledged, snoozed, dismissed or resolved

name: list

description: List the topics this token can read, with how many notifications are open in each.
name: topics

description: Exact number of notifications in each state (active, acknowledged, snoozed, dismissed, resolved), plus inbox (active and acknowledged) and cleared (dismissed and resolved). With keep_cleared_days, also would_remove: how many cleared messages that setting would delete.

keep_cleared_days.description: Preview a keep_cleared_days value before setting it, or "default" with topic to preview dropping that topic's own value

topic.description: With keep_cleared_days, would_remove counts only this topic, to preview a topic_keep_cleared_days value

name: counts

description: Find formatting problems in the newest 500 messages, by topic: Markdown sent as plain text, unknown :shortcodes:, no title, very long messages, raw JSON. Each topic has a count and an example per problem, and a prompt that says how to fix the sender. Fix the sending code with it, then send a test message. With by=sender, one group per topic and sending token. Dismissed findings and topics turned off are left out and listed in dismissed and off.
name: format_check

description: Stop a format_check rule showing for a topic, for one sending token (sender_id from format_check by=sender) or every sender. dismissed=false shows it again. To turn the whole check off for a topic, use set_topic with format_check=false.

dismissed.description: false to show it again; default true

sender_id.description: Sending token id, or "unknown" for the group with no known sender; leave out for every sender

name: format_dismiss

description: Read the server settings, or change them: pass only the fields to change. keep_cleared_days (0 = forever) deletes cleared messages older than that on the next hourly cleanup and needs an admin token; preview it with counts first.

theme.description: The signed-in owner's saved color theme.

theme_colors.description: Six #RRGGBB colors for the custom theme. All required and checked for contrast.

github_hooks_paused.description: Server-wide off switch that pauses every outgoing GitHub issue hook without deleting it (full admin only)

color_rules.description: Card colors, first match wins, on every device. Replaces the whole list: read settings first and send every rule to keep. A rule matches when all its set fields match. Severity preset: [{"priority_min":5,"color":"#DC2626","style":"bar"},{"priority_min":4,"priority_max":4,"color":"#EA580C","style":"bar"},{"priority_min":3,"priority_max":3,"color":"#CA8A04","style":"bar"}]

tag.description: One of its tags; leave out for any

title.description: Text in the title, any case

topic.description: Topic it landed in; leave out for any

favicons.description: Show site icons next to links

keep_cleared_days.description: Days to keep dismissed and resolved messages, counted from when they were cleared; 0 = forever

snooze_default.description: The snooze time a plain tap uses, one of snooze_intervals

snooze_intervals.description: Snooze menu times as durations like 30m or 4h, 1 to 8

swipe_end.description: Buttons the opposite swipe (to the right) reveals. Default [ack]

swipe_start.description: Buttons a swipe toward the start of the line (to the left) reveals on a card, first nearest the edge. Default [clear, snooze]. Each action at most once across swipe_start and swipe_end

topic_keep_cleared_days.description: Per-topic keep_cleared_days, like {"alerts": 7}; null drops a topic's own value so it follows keep_cleared_days again

name: settings

description: Get one notification by its server id, with its current state.
name: get

description: Replace the message of an open notification, keeping its id and state. Use it for progress (step 3 of 10) instead of sending a new one each time.
name: update

description: Mark a notification seen, or actioned with a short note and link, so everyone who reads the topic sees you already dealt with it. It does not clear or change it for anyone. Marking again replaces your mark; no mark removes it.

link.description: Optional http(s) URL, e.g. the issue you filed

mark.description: seen or actioned; leave out to remove your mark

note.description: Optional, at most 200 characters, e.g. filed relay#512

name: mark

description: Acknowledge a notification by its server id.
name: ack

description: Resolve (sender clears) a notification by server id, or by topic plus external_id. Clears it from every device.
name: resolve

description: Snooze a notification by server id.
name: snooze

description: Block until a human acknowledges or dismisses, or the sender resolves the notification, or the timeout passes. Returns reply = the new state, or timeout, and answer = the reply value when one of send's actions was tapped, plus text = what the human typed when that action has text:true.
name: wait_for_reply

description: List every linked device this token can see: id, name, kind (token, browser or phone), linked and last seen times, who may approve (allowed, ask or denied), and whether it can be unlinked.
name: devices
device_theme
description: Set a color theme for a linked device. An empty theme follows its owner's saved choice. Custom uses the owner's saved colors.

id.description: Device id from devices, or this for the calling device

description: Recent links, sign-ins and unlinks of those devices, newest first, with the device that did each.
name: device_log

description: Unlink a browser or phone by its id from devices. It is signed out at once, with every browser it approved.
name: unlink

description: Notification sounds, chosen per device. No arguments lists the valid sound names and the default; devices shows each device's current sound. With id and sound, sets that device's sound.

sound.description: A name from the list, e.g. chime or none

name: sound

description: Which topics reach this person's devices. No arguments lists every readable topic with subscribed, open and last_at; filtered false means this token has no user and sees every topic. An unsubscribed topic is hidden from their lists, counts and pushes, nothing is cleared, and nobody else sees a difference.

for.description: Full admin only: a user id or token id whose topics to read or set

new_topics.description: Whether a topic seen for the first time starts subscribed (default true)

topics.description: Topics to change, like {"chat": false, "infra": true}

name: subscriptions

description: Ask the user to let this token answer approval requests. devices shows its current approve setting. Posts a Confirm prompt on topic; the setting changes only when an allowed device taps Confirm. Returns the prompt: wait_for_reply on its id gives confirm or reject.

approve.description: allowed, or ask (its taps then wait for an allowed device to confirm)

topic.description: Topic for the prompt, default agents; needs publish there

name: request_approve

description: Dismiss (clear) a notification by its server id. It goes away on every device; reopen undoes it.
name: dismiss

description: Make a dismissed, acknowledged, snoozed or resolved notification active again, by its server id.
name: reopen

description: Dismiss every open notification in a topic, or a list of them by server id. Give topic or ids, not both. Returns how many were cleared.
name: clear

description: List silences that have not ended yet.
name: silences

description: Mute a topic, a tag, or a tag in one topic until a set time. Notifications still arrive and sync but do not ring. Give for or until.

tag.description: Tag to mute, in every topic unless topic is set

name: silence

description: End a silence now, by its id from silences.
name: end_silence

description: Set a topic's icon, its check-in timer, or whether format_check looks at it. With checkin, the topic alerts if nothing arrives for that long (a dead man's switch). "" removes the icon or the timer.

device_actions.description: true lets senders add http and broadcast actions, which readers' devices run when tapped. Admin only, off by default

format_check.description: false turns the format check off for this topic, true back on

name: set_topic

description: List a topic's incoming webhook templates, saved and built in. A service posts to /{topic}?template={name}.
name: templates

description: Save an incoming webhook template: how a service's JSON becomes a notification. Fields other than each and secret are Go templates over the posted JSON, like {{.alert.name}}. Needs title or message unless name is a built-in template.

each.description: Dotted path to an array: one notification per item

id.description: Renders to an external id, so the same id updates one notification

priority.description: Renders to 1-5 or min, low, default, high, urgent

resolve.description: Renders to true to resolve the notification with that id

secret.description: Shared secret the service sends; never returned

tags.description: Renders to a comma separated list

name: set_template

description: Delete a saved incoming webhook template.
name: delete_template

description: Dry run an incoming webhook template over a sample payload: returns the notifications a post would publish, stores and sends nothing. Give template to try an unsaved one; otherwise the saved or built-in template named name is used.

headers.description: Request headers the service would send, like X-GitHub-Event

payload.description: The JSON a service would post

template.description: An unsaved template with the set_template fields

name: preview_template

description: List a topic's outgoing webhooks: URLs clrd calls when its notifications are dismissed, acknowledged, resolved, snoozed or an action is tapped. Needs an admin token.
name: hooks

description: Add or replace an outgoing webhook. Saving again turns a failing hook back on. Needs an admin token.

body.description: Optional template for the POST body, for receivers like Slack or Discord: Go template over the sync stream event with get, json (quotes a value) and the incoming template functions, e.g. {"text": {{json .notification.title}}}. Must render valid JSON. Empty sends the event

events.description: Any of dismissed, acknowledged, resolved, snoozed, action; default all

kind.description: discord: url is a Discord webhook URL; each new notification is posted there and a state change edits that message to say who cleared it. Takes no body or secret. slack: url is https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage?channel=CHANNEL and secret is a bot token with chat:write and reactions:write. Posts and edits Slack messages and adds reactions. Takes no body. github: url is https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO and secret a GitHub token that can write issues; each new notification opens an issue (not for anonymous senders or questions, at most 10 an hour), a state change comments on it, a clear or resolve closes it. Empty for a plain webhook

secret.description: Signs each call with HMAC-SHA256; never returned

name: set_hook

description: Dry run an outgoing webhook body template: returns the JSON it would POST for an event, sends nothing. Without event a sample resolved notification on the topic is used. Needs an admin token.

body.description: The body template, as for set_hook

event.description: A sync stream event to render against

name: preview_hook

description: Which private networks and extra ports outgoing webhooks may reach. Empty by default: public addresses on ports 80 and 443 only. Needs an admin token.
name: hook_allow

description: Let outgoing webhooks reach a receiver on a LAN or another port. A dial passes when the address is public or in a listed network, and the port is 80, 443 or listed. Both lists are required; empty lists turn it off. Refused when the server operator set CLRD_HOOK_ALLOW=off. Needs an admin token.

networks.description: CIDR ranges like 192.168.1.0/24, or single addresses

name: set_hook_allow

description: Delete an outgoing webhook. Needs an admin token.
name: delete_hook

description: Recent calls of one outgoing webhook, with status and error. Needs an admin token.
name: hook_deliveries

description: List API tokens (never their secrets). Needs an admin token.
name: tokens

description: Create an API token for a phone, script or agent. The secret is in the result once and never again. It starts denied for approval requests; raise it with request_approve or from an allowed device. Limit it with topics, or with grants (per-topic scopes, first match wins), not both. Needs an admin token.

grants.description: Per-topic rules, like [{"topic":"home-*","scopes":["publish"]}]; each grant's scopes must be in scopes

topics.description: Topics it may use; leave out for every topic

name: create_token

description: Revoke an API token by its id from tokens. Its open streams close at once. Needs an admin token.
name: revoke_token

description: Rename an API token by its id from tokens (a sender's token_id). Needs an admin token.
name: rename_token

description: Give an API token a new secret, in the result once as token. Same id, so its sender rules, history and grants stay. The old secret stops at once, and browsers and phones signed in with it are signed out. Typed-in tokens only. Needs an admin token.
name: rotate_token

description: Invite an agent: one short single-use string it claims to get its own user and token, held to these topics (read and publish) and denied for approval requests. Returns invite (clrd://agent?...) and url (https form; a GET gives the agent a plain-text guide). Hand either to the agent, privately: whoever claims it first gets the access. Needs an admin token.

expires_in.description: How long the invite lives, 1m to 1h, default 15m

name.description: The agent's name, unique among users

topics.description: Topics it may use; a pattern like home-* is allowed

name: create_agent_invite

description: List users: people who own device tokens, each with its grants (null limits nothing). Needs an admin token.
name: users

description: Create a user (a person). Attach tokens with set_token_user; every device of the user then follows its grants. Leave grants out for a user that limits nothing. Needs an admin token.

grants.description: Per-topic rules, like [{"topic":"family","scopes":["read"]}]; read and publish only. null limits nothing, [] is no topic

name: create_user

description: Set which topics a user's devices may read or publish, first match wins. To share a topic with someone, give their user a grant on it. null limits nothing, [] is no topic. Their open streams reconnect under the new rules. Needs an admin token.

grants.description: Per-topic rules, like [{"topic":"family","scopes":["read"]}]; read and publish only. null limits nothing, [] is no topic

name: set_user_grants

description: Delete a user with no tokens attached. Needs an admin token.
name: delete_user

description: Attach a typed-in token (and every browser and phone made from it) to a user, or detach it with user "". Needs an admin token.

user.description: User id, or empty to detach

name: set_token_user

description: Create a Gotify app key for one topic, for senders built for Gotify (shoutrrr, Watchtower, the gotify CLI). The key is in the result once; it only publishes, only to that topic, only on POST /message. Revoke it with revoke_token and the result's token_id. Needs an admin token.

name.description: App name, the title when a message has none

priority.description: Gotify priority 0 to 10 for messages that send none; leave out for clrd's default

name: create_gotify_app

description: Create a Pushover app key for one topic, for senders built for Pushover (Apprise, scripts). The key is in the result once, with a user value for senders that require one (clrd never checks it); the key only publishes, only to that topic, only on POST /1/messages.json. Revoke it with revoke_token and the result's token_id. Needs an admin token.

name.description: App name, the title when a message has none

name: create_pushover_app

description: Whether ntfy routes take requests with no credentials, and on which topics. Off unless set. Needs an admin token.
name: ntfy_anonymous

description: Set the topics anyone may use with no credentials, on ntfy routes only (the native API always needs a token). Like ntfy's everyone rules, e.g. [{"topic":"up*","scopes":["publish"]}] for UnifiedPush. An empty list turns it off. Open anonymous streams reconnect under the new rules. Needs an admin token.

grants.description: Per-topic rules, first match wins; scopes are read and/or publish, empty to deny

scopes.description: read, publish, or empty to deny

name: set_ntfy_anonymous

description: Which other web sites may use the ntfy and Gotify routes from a browser. Empty by default: only clrd's own pages, phones and scripts. Needs an admin token.
name: ntfy_origins

description: Set the web sites (origins like https://ntfy.sh, or "*" for any site, as ntfy answers) whose pages may publish and subscribe on the ntfy and Gotify routes from a browser. An empty list allows only clrd's own pages; phones and scripts are never affected. Needs an admin token.
name: set_ntfy_origins

description: Every CLRD_* environment setting in effect, defaults filled in. Read only: these change by setting the variable and restarting. Needs an admin token.
name: server_env

description: This server's clrd version, build commit and date, and its recent history (what changed in each version, newest first), with a link to the full history. Any token.
name: version

description: ntfy publish options senders used that clrd accepts but ignores (email, call and the like), with counts, so a migrated sender can be fixed. Needs an admin token.
name: ntfy_ignored

description: Every service or token that has published, most recently heard first: name, kind, webhook template, User-Agent and address hints, first and last seen, message count per topic. Found on its first message, no setup. Needs an admin token without a topic list.
name: senders

description: Traffic numbers for the last days (default 7): total, answered, priorities, UTC hourly counts, weekday-by-hour counts in the server's local time, top topics and senders with previous-period counts, clearers and time to clear, repeat alerts, and delivery failures. Includes total and same-token clears, current quiet alarms, and live client streams. Needs an admin token without a topic list.

days.description: How many days back from now, 1 to 366

group.description: Split UTC hourly counts by topic, sender or priority

name: stats

description: One sender from senders, by its id, with its recent notifications that are still stored.
name: sender

description: Set a sender's rules: pause (accept and drop), mute (store, never alert), a priority floor and cap, routes from the topic it names to other topics, an alarm when it goes quiet, and an icon for its publishes that give none. Only the fields given change; routes, when given, replace them all. Each change is kept and can be undone. Needs an admin token without a topic list.

alert_topic.description: Topic for that alarm; "" for where its last topic routes

expect.description: Raise an urgent alarm when it sends nothing for this long, 1m to 8784h like "25h"; "" for off

icon.description: http(s) image URL its publishes get when they give none, before the topic's icon; "" for none

id.description: Sender id, or the id of a token that has not published yet

routes.description: Topic it names (or "*") to a list of topics, like {"*":["infra"]}; [] drops; {} clears every route

name: set_sender

description: A sender's rule changes, newest first: before, after, who and when.
name: sender_changes

description: Put a sender's rules back to how they were before one change from sender_changes; recorded as a new change.
name: undo_sender_change

description: Get the VAPID public key and subscription status for this read token.
name: push

description: Register this read token's browser PushSubscription JSON after the user grants notification permission. Subscription data is sensitive.
name: set_push

description: Remove this read token's Web Push subscription from the server.
name: delete_push
